title: One hard product, two easy ones
hook: 13 × 7 is awkward. Cut the rectangle somewhere clever and it stops being awkward.

knows: area of a rectangle is width times height
doesNotKnow: that a hard product splits into easy ones

misconception: 13 × 7 must be done as a single step; bigger factors need a different method.
objective: The learner can explain that a rectangle can be cut anywhere and the two areas add up to the whole, so a product can be split into easy products.

claims.text: A rectangle cut into two pieces has area equal to the sum of the pieces' areas, so a(b + c) = ab + ac.
claims.source: Distributive law, area model: a rectangle of width b + c and height a is two rectangles of widths b and c and height a.

claims.text: 13 × 7 = 91, and cutting at 10 gives 10 × 7 = 70 and 3 × 7 = 21, which add to 91.
claims.source: Recomputed in node: 13*7 = 91; 10*7 + 3*7 = 70 + 21 = 91 (Demo.tsx LEN, ROWS, TEN).

claims.text: Whatever column the cut is placed at, the two pieces add to the same total, 91; the reveal quotes the last cut other than 10 that the learner stopped on (a −1/+1 press or the slider resting 300 ms), as a × 7 + (13 − a) × 7 = 91.
claims.source: a × 7 + (13 − a) × 7 = 13 × 7 for every a from 1 to 12; stop() and move() in Demo.tsx v3. | a x 7 + (13 - a) x 7 = 13 x 7 for every a from 1 to 12; the stage computes both pieces from the slider value. | REOPENED 2026-10-14 (v3, wave D r5 revision by demo-builder): learner-visible sentence changed; needs a fresh check. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Pass 22 re-check of v3: a x 7 + (13-a) x 7 = 91 for a = 1..12 (node). The reveal quotes `other`, set by stop() on a +/-1 press or a 300 ms slider rest, as "${a*7} + ${(13-a)*7} = 91" (products, not the a x 7 form written in the claim).

claims.text: Multiplying by 10 is easy, so a cut at 10 makes the easiest products.
claims.source: Place value: multiplying by 10 appends a zero. A teaching judgement, not a theorem.

recall.question: To work out 14 × 6 in your head by cutting a rectangle, which split is easiest?
recall.why: Cut 14 into 10 and 4: 10 × 6 + 4 × 6 = 60 + 24 = 84. Other cuts also work, but 10 × 6 is easy.
